oewn-10269647-n.learner: a person whose job is the law, who is allowed to work in it and who takes cases to court or gives advice about the law
examples: Her father had been an attorney in Meryton, and had left her four thousand pounds.

oewn-00119088-n.learner: a sudden redness that comes into your face, for example when you feel embarrassed, guilty, ashamed or shy
examples: Once or twice she could discern a faint blush; but in general Charlotte wisely did not hear.
Their eyes instantly met, and the cheeks of each were overspread with the deepest blush.

oewn-14074353-n.learner: a pink colour, especially in the cheeks, that is seen as a sign that someone is healthy
examples: After a week in the country air, the healthy blush was back in her cheeks.

oewn-04119846-n.learner: a pink or red powder that people put on their cheeks as makeup
examples: She brushed a little blush onto her cheeks before going out.

oewn-00291174-r.learner: in a short and clear way, using only a few words
examples: These causes must be stated, though briefly.
To Mr. Bennet's acknowledgments he briefly replied, with assurances of his eagerness to promote the welfare of any of his family
She stopped briefly at the door and then went in.

oewn-00358006-a.learner: typical of a person or thing, or marking it out as different from others
examples: The manner in which they spoke of the Meryton assembly was sufficiently characteristic.
She looks sickly and cross.
to say the truth, I was too cross to write.

oewn-01448808-s.learner: going or lying across something, at right angles to its long side
examples: Here, leading the way through every walk and cross walk

oewn-00968795-a.learner: well known, or easy to recognize
examples: neither the carriage, nor the livery of the servant who preceded it, were familiar to them.

oewn-01310022-s.learner: knowing a lot about something, or knowing it very well (usually followed by 'with')
examples: There is a very fine old saying, which everybody here is of course familiar with

oewn-00973438-a.learner: part of normal everyday life; common and ordinary, not strange
examples: The little shop sold familiar things like bread, soap and matches.

oewn-00109415-r.learner: to this place, especially toward the person who is speaking
examples: If he fears me, why come hither?
You can be at no loss, Miss Bennet, to understand the reason of my journey hither.

oewn-00287080-a.learner: not pushed unfairly toward one side, and not holding opinions formed before knowing the facts
examples: I believed it on impartial conviction, as truly as I wished it in reason.

oewn-01727525-a.learner: not showing that you like or help one person or side more than another
examples: A judge must be impartial and treat both sides in the same way.

oewn-02725274-v.learner: to tend to do or be something, or to lean that way in your nature or mind
examples: For my part, I am inclined to believe it all Mr. Darcy's
I am much more inclined than I was to judge as your eldest sister does of the matter.

oewn-01776093-v.learner: to feel in favour of something, or willing to do it
examples: After the way he had spoken to her, she was not inclined to help him.

oewn-00682760-v.learner: to make someone willing or ready to accept an action, an attitude or a belief
examples: His honest face inclined her to believe his story.

oewn-02066946-v.learner: to lower or bend your head or the top part of your body, as when you nod or bow
examples: He inclined his head politely as she passed.
The road inclines steeply down toward the river.

oewn-02175766-v.learner: to bend or turn your ear toward someone who is speaking so that you can hear them well
examples: She inclined her ear to the old man to catch his quiet words.

oewn-00745603-n.learner: a wrong that is unfairly done to someone and goes against their rights
examples: I have no such injuries to resent.
Attention, forbearance, patience with Darcy, was injury to Wickham.

oewn-14309164-n.learner: any harm done to the body by violence, an accident, a broken bone and so on, or the state of being hurt in this way
examples: He could not play for a month because of a knee injury.

oewn-07328236-n.learner: an accident in which something or someone is physically damaged or hurt
examples: The report lists every injury that happened on the building site last year.

oewn-00745741-n.learner: an act that causes someone or something to be physically damaged
examples: The deliberate injury of animals is against the law.

oewn-07354849-n.learner: a case of a soldier or other member of the armed forces being hurt in fighting
examples: The army reported twelve deaths and forty injuries after the battle.
